detailed_findings.finding: The map φ(Λ, x) = Λ \ {x} is shown to land in genus-(h+1) numerical semigroups by proving closure under addition using minimality of x, cofiniteness, and the fact that x > F(Λ), which also yields F(φ(Λ, x)) = x.

The inverse map ψ(S) = (S ∪ {F(S)}, F(S)) is fully justified: closure of S ∪ {F(S)} is checked by cases, genus drops by one, and F(S) is proved to be an effective minimal generator of the enlarged semigroup.
The cardinality identity |A| = Σ e(Λ) and the regrouping Σ e(Λ) = Σ_r r·n_h(r) are correct given the explicit finiteness assumptions in the lemma statement.

reason: The proof is mathematically complete and matches the lemma sketch closely. It constructs the standard bijection between pairs (Λ, x) with Λ of genus h and x an effective generator, and numerical semigroups S of genus h+1 obtained by removing/adding the Frobenius element. Both directions are checked carefully: numerical semigroup axioms, genus shift by one, identification of the Frobenius number, minimality of the added element, and effectiveness. The final counting argument and regrouping by the values r = e(Λ) are correct under the stated finiteness assumptions.
